patch.value: Preserve bisect reports when the culprit is a shallow boundary

A bisect verdict whose first bad commit is a shallow merge parent cannot be enriched because linkedItems unconditionally reads the omitted first parent. Range construction succeeds, but manual bad and subsequent status return object_not_found. This is a separate provenance-reporting path discovered during PR 131 review round 3, beyond the requested ancestry and checkout fixes.

A real shallow-merge regression covers bad/run/status when the first bad commit has an omitted parent; available explicit associations remain available; missing provenance has an honest omission or boundary receipt; complete-history and root-commit reports remain correct.

Create an empty-tree ancestor A, good G with parent A, side S with parent A, and merge M with parents G and S. Clone M with depth 2 so A is absent and G/S are shallow. Initialize a real tracker and linked test in the clone. Start bisect G M, mark S bad, then request status.
Keep the core bisect conclusion available and report unavailable file-derived attribution explicitly instead of throwing or inventing provenance.
Start succeeds; marking S bad and later status both fail with No object for the omitted first-parent commit. The disposable reproduction verified the parent object is absent.
